T5852444a4c9d322c.SUPPORT: CPC 53 deems ancestral property in hands of a son liable for the debt of a deceased ancestor if a decree has been passed.
T5852444a4c9d322c.OPPOSITION: The decree specifically mentions the 'estate of Baldev Das deceased,' which appellants argue restricts liability to property owned at death.
T5852444a4c9d322c.EXCEPTION: The debt must not be immoral, and the sons' share must be liable under Hindu law for the pre-partition debt.

T8b2a03644ed7cd5f.SUPPORT: A 1928 partition decree legally severed joint family property, allotting specific shops to the sons' share.
T8b2a03644ed7cd5f.OPPOSITION: The decree was obtained after partition, but the debt was contracted by the father prior to it.
T8b2a03644ed7cd5f.EXCEPTION: Under Hindu law, the separate share obtained on partition is liable for the pre-partition debt if not immoral.

T624c686329396ce9.SUPPORT: The plaintiff gave up the claim for a mortgage decree against the properties in suit, satisfied only with a money decree against Baldev Das personally.
T624c686329396ce9.OPPOSITION: The compromise decree was passed against the 'estate of Baldev Das deceased in possession of his legal representatives.'
T624c686329396ce9.EXCEPTION: The waiver of the mortgage claim does not necessarily limit execution to the father's estate if the debt is ancestral.

Tcdd225f57f64f8a2.SUPPORT: The Subordinate Judge found the debt was not immoral and the sons' share was liable under Hindu law.
Tcdd225f57f64f8a2.OPPOSITION: The appellants did not raise a petition alleging the debt was tainted with immorality.
Tcdd225f57f64f8a2.EXCEPTION: The lower court's finding on immorality is binding unless overturned on appeal.

Tdb7213c4fe1ba62a.SUPPORT: The phrase 'estate of Baldev Das deceased' must mean property belonging to him at the date of his death.
Tdb7213c4fe1ba62a.OPPOSITION: CPC 53 treats property liable under Hindu law as property of the deceased which has come to the hands of the son.
Tdb7213c4fe1ba62a.EXCEPTION: The statutory deeming provision overrides the literal interpretation of 'estate' in the decree.

T85449ce5943bdfba.SUPPORT: A pious obligation for a pre-partition debt can be enforced against the sons' separate property.
T85449ce5943bdfba.OPPOSITION: Such obligation could be enforced only in a properly constituted suit and not by way of execution of a decree obtained against the father alone.
T85449ce5943bdfba.EXCEPTION: Execution proceedings are permissible if the property is deemed the legal representative's under CPC 53.

Tffe5412eb591a7dc.SUPPORT: There was no petition of compromise filed by the parties and made part of the decree.
Tffe5412eb591a7dc.OPPOSITION: There are two statements on the record setting out the terms of the compromise.
Tffe5412eb591a7dc.EXCEPTION: The absence of a formal petition does not invalidate the decree if the terms are clear from the statements.

Ta23bd2bc1e7b0641.SUPPORT: Questions arising between parties relating to execution, discharge, or satisfaction of the decree shall be determined by the Court executing the decree.
Ta23bd2bc1e7b0641.OPPOSITION: Substantive liability for the debt requires its own basis under Hindu law and CPC 53.
Ta23bd2bc1e7b0641.EXCEPTION: The executing court determines procedural execution issues, not the substantive validity of the debt itself.

Tebb6582bfcf623de.SUPPORT: Baldev Das was the deceased ancestor who contracted the debt prior to partition.
Tebb6582bfcf623de.OPPOSITION: The debt was contracted before the partition, but the decree was obtained after.
Tebb6582bfcf623de.EXCEPTION: The timing of the decree does not negate the ancestral nature of the debt.

T1e3785809c4af80f.SUPPORT: The appellants (sons) hold the specified partitioned property.
T1e3785809c4af80f.OPPOSITION: The property was allotted to the sons' share on partition.
T1e3785809c4af80f.EXCEPTION: Holding the property does not automatically exempt it from ancestral debt liability.

Te1eee3d9624a4f54.SUPPORT: Independent substantive Hindu law makes the sons' share liable for the father's pre-partition debt.
Te1eee3d9624a4f54.OPPOSITION: CPC 53 itself does not establish this condition; it only deems the property as received by the legal representative.
Te1eee3d9624a4f54.EXCEPTION: The deeming provision relies on the substantive law of Hindu liability.

T7e2b04c2fe9a176f.SUPPORT: The appellants and the decree holder have the required suit-party or representative status.
T7e2b04c2fe9a176f.OPPOSITION: The appellants were made parties only as legal representatives after the father's death.
T7e2b04c2fe9a176f.EXCEPTION: Legal representative status is sufficient for execution proceedings under CPC 47.

T73ed27d6137a3002.SUPPORT: The precise question concerns execution, discharge, or satisfaction of the decree.
T73ed27d6137a3002.OPPOSITION: The objection relates to the liability of the sons' separate property for the father's debt.
T73ed27d6137a3002.EXCEPTION: This falls within the scope of questions to be determined by the executing court under CPC 47.
